items.title: [Bug]: Cache hit rate drops from ~89% with DRAM only to ~76% with SSD enabled (v0.3.14-rc1, DeepSeek-V4-Flash, vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0)
items.author: Eric-dot
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

## Summary

I am running **DeepSeek-V4-Flash** with **vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0** and **Mooncake v0.3.14-rc1**. With a workload of **128K input tokens and a 90% shared prefix**, cache reuse is normal when only the **L2 DRAM pool** is enabled: the inference engine reports an **external hit rate of approximately 89%**.

However, when I enable SSD pooling/offload in addition to DRAM, the reported overall cache hit rate drops to approximately **76%**, substantially below both the DRAM-only baseline and the 90% shared-prefix ratio.

**The key observation is that enabling the additional SSD tier reduces the observed cache hit rate: DRAM-only gives ~89%, while DRAM + SSD gives ~76% for this workload.** This is a cache-reuse question, rather than just a concern about SSD read latency.

## Environment

- Mooncake: [v0.3.14-rc1](https://github.com/kvcache-ai/Mooncake/tree/v0.3.14-rc1)
- Inference framework: vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0
- Model: DeepSeek-V4-Flash
- Mooncake protocol: `ascend`
- Input length: 128K tokens
- Shared/common prefix: 90% of the input
- Configured `global_segment_size`: `40GB` (see DRAM-only configuration below)

Here, "L2" means the DRAM pooling tier in my deployment.

## Observed comparison

| Configuration | Observed hit rate |
| --- | --- |
| L2 DRAM pooling only; SSD disabled | External hit rate ~89% |
| DRAM pooling with SSD pooling/offload enabled | Reported overall hit rate ~76% |

This is a drop of approximately **13 percentage points** after enabling SSD.

## DRAM-only baseline configuration

```json
{
    "metadata_server": "P2PHANDSHAKE",
    "protocol": "ascend",
    "device_name": "",
    "master_server_address": "<master_ip>:50088",
    "global_segment_size": "40GB",
    "preferred_segment": false,
    "prefer_alloc_in_same_node": true,
    "enable_ssd_offload": false,
    "ssd_offload_path": "/nvme/mooncake_offload",
    "tenant_id": "default"
}
```

**This JSON is the DRAM-only baseline (`enable_ssd_offload: false`), not the configuration of the SSD-enabled run.** The complete SSD-enabled configuration and master/client launch commands are not included in this initial report.

## Reproduction scenario

1. Run DeepSeek-V4-Flash using vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0 and Mooncake v0.3.14-rc1.
2. Exercise a workload with 128K-token inputs and a 90% common prefix using only L2 DRAM pooling. Observe an external hit rate of approximately 89%.
3. Enable SSD pooling/offload and run the same workload. Observe the reported overall cache hit rate dropping to approximately 76%.

These are the observed comparison steps; a standalone reproduction script, request concurrency, request count, warm-up procedure, and exact metric calculation are not available in this initial report.

## Expected behavior / questions

I would expect cache reuse with SSD enabled to remain close to the ~89% DRAM-only baseline for this shared-prefix workload, assuming adequate capacity and completed cache writes. I understand that a 90% shared prefix does not by itself guarantee an exact 90% measured hit rate.

Could maintainers help clarify:

1. Is this hit-rate reduction a known issue or expected behavior with Mooncake v0.3.14-rc1 and vLLM-Ascend v0.30.0?
2. Are there SSD offload, eviction, read-back, or connector settings required to preserve the DRAM-only reuse rate?
3. Does enabling SSD change how the external/overall cache hit rate is accounted for in this integration, or should these measurements be directly comparable?
4. Which logs and counters would best distinguish failed cache writes, SSD read-back failures, eviction effects, and metric-accounting differences?

## Logs and related reports

Logs are currently on another machine and are not attached. I cannot yet confirm whether `BatchPut failed`, `INVALID_KEY`, or `OBJECT_ALREADY_EXISTS` occurs in this deployment, so I am not attributing the regression to a specific cause.

I searched existing issues and found related reports, but could not establish that they describe the same problem:

- #3331: Incomplete SSD-backed KV reuse after eviction with MooncakeStoreConnector; a different Mooncake version/model, with reported BatchPut allocation failures.
- #4740: Partial SSD offload buckets lose task ownership across heartbeat cycles.
- #2799: DeepSeek-V4 SSD offload read failures with `INVALID_KEY`.

I am opening this report to capture the specific **DRAM-only ~89% vs. SSD-enabled ~76%** comparison on the versions and workload above. Please let me know if it should be tracked under an existing issue.

items.title: [dynamo] Compiled code silently gets the wrong `__name__` for functions decorated with `functools.wraps` (regression in 2.15)
items.author: peterdsharpe
items.body_excerpt:
### 🐛 Describe the bug

While adding `torch.compile` coverage to TensorDict's CI, I noticed that in-place math on one of our types compiles on torch 2.14.1 but fails on the 2.15.0 release candidate (pytorch/tensordict#2787). Chasing that down the rabbit hole led me to believe that the issue is actually in Dynamo: inside compiled code, a function's `__name__` now comes from its code object, so a name set by `functools.wraps` is lost. TensorDict happened to get an `AttributeError` out of it, but in general nothing errors, and the compiled code just uses the wrong string.

I think this should be fixed before 2.15.0 ships, since it's a silent wrong result, and plenty of code dispatches on or logs `fn.__name__`. Expected behavior is that compiled code sees the same `__name__` as eager, as it does on 2.14.1.

```python
import functools
import torch

def deco(func):
    @functools.wraps(func)
    def new_func(x):
        return func(x)
    return new_func

@deco
def add_(x):
    return x + 1

def f(x, method=add_):
    return x + len(method.__name__)

x = torch.zeros(1)
print(f(x))                                 # tensor([4.]), len("add_")
print(torch.compile(f, fullgraph=True)(x))  # tensor([8.]) on 2.15.0, len("new_func")
```

I had an agent investigate further; below is the AI-assisted analysis.

### Error logs

None. The compiled function returns a different value, with no error and no graph break.

### AI-assisted analysis

An AI coding agent (Claude, in the Pi harness) bisected the nightlies and read the Dynamo source at my request. I reviewed its findings before filing.

> Bisected on the CPU nightlies with the script above: 2.15.0.dev20260903 (7c31c89) is the last good build, and 2.15.0.dev20260904 (3780801) the first bad one.
>
> In that window, #193983 ("Model readonly members by making `setter` a required arg in `Member`") removed the `_fn_getattr` getters of `UserFunctionVariable` for `__name__`, `__qualname__`, `__code__`, `__defaults__`, `__kwdefaults__`, `__annotations__`, `__type_params__`, `__doc__`, `__module__` and `__closure__`. These attributes now come from `BaseUserFunctionVariable.tp_getset` in `torch/_dynamo/variables/functions.py`, whose `__name__` getter calls `get_name()`, which returns `self.get_code().co_name`.
>
> The same check for each attribute that `functools.wraps` copies, or that can be assigned on a plain function:
>
> | Attribute | 2.14.1 | 2.15.0 RC and nightly 2.16.0.dev20261015 |
> |---|---|---|
> | `__name__`, from `functools.wraps` or assigned | eager value | the name of the code object |
> | `__doc__`, from `functools.wraps` or assigned | eager value | `None` |
> | `__module__`, assigned | eager value | the module of the function's globals |
> | `__qualname__`, from `functools.wraps` or assigned | already wrong | wrong |
>
> `backend="eager"` gives the same results, so the bug is in Dynamo, not Inductor. The open PR #196887 reads `__name__` and `__qualname__` from the function object again, which would fix those two, but not `__doc__` or `__module__`.

### Versions

Root cause: `BaseUserFunctionVariable.get_name()` returns `self.get_code().co_name`. items.title: Block-wise Scatter-Reduce :  __getitem__ / __setitem__ errors
items.author: olivier-peltre
items.body_excerpt:
While trying to implement a scatter-add reduction inside a kernel, I get errors related to `tensor.__{get,set}item__`. 

As far as I understand, indexing features in triton are either limited or new and I'd like some advice on how to find a satisfactory workaround :slightly_smiling_face: 

Here is a sample code and descriptions of errors: 

```py
    ...
    # load indices and values
    idx = tl.load(idx_ptr + j + row)
    values = tl.load(values_ptr + begin + block)     
    # prepare output 
    out = tl.zeros((BLOCK_HEIGHT, OUT_WIDTH), values.dtype)
    mask = tl.full((OUT_WIDTH,), 0, tl.int1)

    # reduce on axis -1 in horizontal for-loop (FAILS) 
    offset = idx[0]
    for k in tl.static_range(BLOCK_WIDTH): 
        idx_k = idx[k] - offset
        mask[idx_k] = 1 
        out[:,idx_k] += values[:,k]
    
    # store output (atomic lock in case of small global height)
    tl.atomic_add(out_ptr + idx_0, out, mask) 
```
- when trying to access indices I get e.g.  line `offset = idx[0]` I get: 
    ```
    > `offset = idx[0]`
    ValueError("unsupported tensor index: constexpr[0]")
    ```
    is this intended?
    
    I can obviously replace this by `tl.load(idx_ptr + j (+k))`  as workaround
    
- I further get upon calling setitem:
    ```
    > mask[idx_k] = 1
    AssertionError()
    ```
    Overlooking the source, I guess this is because `tensor` doesn't have a `__setitem__` method, though throwing `AttributeError` would be more informative.
    
- I assume the following
  ```
  out[:, idx_k] += val[:,k]
  ```
  would fail for the same reason, though I could probably work around this with `tl.where`.  I'm also unsure whether the shared memory (?) accumulator `out` shouldn't be transposed for performance befor the final `store` instruction. 
  

But more generally, what would you recommend? Maybe this has been done somewhere else? 
Any form of advice greatly appreciated :pray: 

I'm tagging you here @apgoucher and @Mogball, as I wonder whether your recent #5262 PR could help on this subject. 


### Note

I'm looking into whether triton could help scale-up scatter-add kernels, after having noticed large runtime discrepancies between jax and torch implementations (torch ~4x faster) though both scale bad to large input sizes. I'm hoping that aligning loads to 128B sector sizes while putting more work on each warp (as opposed to a naive implementation relying solely on atomics) could improve the scaling in the large input size limit.

I'm also wondering whether leveraging cuda `__shfl_sync` semantics wouldn't be necessary to get satisfactory results on this (which would probably fall out of triton's scope). Though I'm still looking for a good triton implementation first!

items.title: Python 3.14t: C extension missing Py_MOD_GIL declaration causes GIL re-enable warning
items.author: kdt2014
items.body_excerpt:
### Description
Triton 3.5.0 provides binary wheels for Python 3.14t (free-threaded build), but the C extension module `triton._C.libtriton` does not declare GIL compatibility, causing Python to re-enable the GIL with a warning.

### Environment
- Python version: 3.14.0 free-threading build
- Triton version: 3.5.0
- Platform: Linux x86_64
- Installation: `pip install triton` (cp314t wheel)

### Current Behavior
When importing Triton in Python 3.14t:
```python
import triton._C.libtriton
```

Output:
```
RuntimeWarning: The global interpreter lock (GIL) has been enabled to load module 
'triton._C.libtriton', which has not declared that it can run safely without the GIL.
```

### Expected Behavior
The C extension should declare its GIL compatibility status using the `Py_mod_gil` slot in the module definition, as described in [PEP 703](https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/).

### Reproduction Steps
```bash
python3.14t -c "import triton._C.libtriton"
```

### Suggested Fix
Add the appropriate `Py_mod_gil` declaration in the C extension module initialization:
```c
static PyModuleDef_Slot module_slots[] = {
    {Py_mod_gil, Py_MOD_GIL_NOT_USED},  // or Py_MOD_GIL_USED if needed
    {0, NULL}
};
```

### Additional Context
- Since Triton already builds and distributes cp314t wheels, adding the GIL declaration would complete the free-threaded support
- This affects users trying to leverage true parallel execution in Python 3.14t
- The warning can be suppressed with `PYTHON_GIL=0`, but proper declaration is the correct solution

### References
- PEP 703: https://peps.python.org/pep-0703/
- Python 3.14 free-threading docs: https://docs.python.org/3.14/howto/free-threading-extensions.html
```

items.title: Compiler crash:LLVM AMDGPU MachineVerifier report "Virtual register defs don't dominate all uses"
items.author: O1iveira7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling a legal, deterministic Triton GEMM kernel aborts the process during LLVM AMDGPU codegen: LLVM's post-RA MachineVerifier rejects the generated MIR and calls `abort()`. The same kernel compiles and runs correctly with `num_warps=2` or `num_stages=1/3`; the crash requires `num_warps=1, num_stages=2`.
**Likely cause**
`num_stages=2` enables software pipelining, which clones the A-tile address computation (`V_XOR_B32_e32 112, %3212`) into the prologue and the loop body. A late machine pass (register allocation / live-range splitting / COPY insertion) then makes both clones define the same virtual register `%9951`, without materializing one definition at a common dominator. The epilogue use is reachable from a path that bypasses each definition (bb.4 bypasses the loop-body def in bb.5; bb.1 bypasses the prologue def in bb.2), so no def dominates the use and MachineVerifier aborts. Correct behavior would be distinct vregs per path, or a single merged definition at the common dominator (bb.3).

**Error log excerpt**
Output before crash
REPRO_START M=31 N=63 K=33 BLOCK=128x128x32 num_warps=1 num_stages=2 grid=(1, 1)

LLVM MachineVerifier error (process SIGABRT, exit code 134)
*** Bad machine code: Virtual register defs don't dominate all uses. ***
- function:      gemm
- v. register:   %9951
LLVM ERROR: Found 1 machine code errors.

Definitions/uses of bad virtual register %9951
```
1952:  bb.2   %9951:vgpr_32 = COPY %9347:vgpr_32       def 1 (prologue path)
2254:  bb.5   %9951:vgpr_32 = COPY %9346:vgpr_32       def 2 (loop-body path)
3346:  bb.9   %9348:vgpr_32 = COPY %9951:vgpr_32       use 1 (inside loop; reachable only via bb.5)
4244:  bb.15  %9349:vgpr_32 = COPY %9951:vgpr_32       use 2 (epilogue; reachable via both bb.4/bb.5 paths)
```


Sources of the two definitions
(the same A-tile address computation was cloned twice by software pipelining)
1951:  %9347:vgpr_32 = V_XOR_B32_e32 112, %3212:vgpr_32, ...; 22_gemm_llvm_verifier_min_repro.py:56:18
2253:  %9346:vgpr_32 = V_XOR_B32_e32 112, %3212:vgpr_32

Dominance relationship (two incoming paths to bb.15)
```
bb.3 -> bb.5 -> (loop: bb.7..bb.9) -> bb.10 -> bb.6 -> ... -> bb.15
bb.3 -> bb.4 -> bb.6 -> ... -> bb.15
```
def 2 is in bb.5, but the bb.4 path bypasses bb.5; def 1 is in bb.2, but another path via bb.1 bypasses bb.2
=> the use in bb.15 has no dominating definition, so the verifier is correct to reject it

Exit code
134 (SIGABRT)

**Reproducer**
```
import os

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def gemm(_fz_switch_ptr, _fz_switch_output_ptr, A, B, C, M, N, K, BLOCK_M: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_N: tl.constexpr, BLOCK_K: tl.constexpr):
    opaque_values = tl.load(_fz_switch_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2))
    opaque_zero, opaque_one = tl.split(opaque_values)
    opaque_true = opaque_zero < opaque_one
    n_id = tl.program_id(1)
    a_offset_m = tl.arange(0, BLOCK_M)
    acc = tl.zeros((BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N), dtype=tl.float32)
    for k in range(0, K, BLOCK_K):
        offset_k = k + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_K)
        a_tile = tl.load(A + a_offset_m[:, None] * K + offset_k[None, :], mask=(a_offset_m[:, None] < M) & (offset_k[None, :] < K), other=0.0)
        if opaque_true:
            tl.store(_fz_switch_output_ptr + tl.arange(0, 2), tl.min(tl.reshape(tl.arange(0, 4), (2, 2)) + opaque_one, axis=1) + opaque_values)
        b_tile = tl.load(B + (n_id * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N))[None, :] + offset_k[:, None] * N, mask=((n_id * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N))[None, :] < N) & (offset_k[:, None] < K), other=0.0)
        acc += tl.dot(a_tile, b_tile)
    if opaque_true:
        tl.store(C + a_offset_m[:, None] * N + (n_id * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N))[None, :], acc.to(tl.float16), mask=(a_offset_m[:, None] < M) & ((n_id * BLOCK_N + tl.arange(0, BLOCK_N))[None, :] < N))


def _main() -> None:
    device = "cuda"  # ROCm uses the cuda namespace; no CPU fallback possible.
    M, N, K = 31, 63, 33
    num_warps = int(os.environ.get("NUM_WARPS", "1"))
    num_stages = int(os.environ.get("NUM_STAGES", "2"))
    BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K = 128, 128, 32

    torch.manual_seed(0)
    a = torch.rand(M, K, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    b = torch.rand(K, N, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    c = torch.rand(M, N, device=device, dtype=torch.float32)
    switch = torch.tensor([0, 1], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    scratch = torch.empty(2, dtype=torch.float32, device=device)

    grid = (triton.cdiv(M, BLOCK_M), triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N))
    print(
        f"REPRO_START M={M} N={N} K={K} BLOCK={BLOCK_M}x{BLOCK_N}x{BLOCK_K} "
        f"num_warps={num_warps} num_stages={num_stages} grid={grid}",
        flush=True,
    )
    gemm[grid](
        switch, scratch, a, b, c, M, N, K,
        BLOCK_M=BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K=BLOCK_K,
        num_warps=num_warps, num_stages=num_stages,
    )
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print("REPRO_DONE (no crash; use NUM_WARPS=1 NUM_STAGES=2 to trigger)", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()

### Environment details

```

- ROCm 7.2.3

- triton-rocm 3.8.0.

items.title: [Gluon] Warp-specialized lowering emits different setmaxnreg instructions within one warpgroup
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

**Summary.** When a warp-specialized kernel sets `worker_num_regs` and a warpgroup holds more than one partition, the warps of that warpgroup execute different `setmaxnreg` instructions, although PTX ISA 9.4 §9.7.21.5 (`setmaxnreg`) requires all warps of a warpgroup to execute the same `setmaxnreg` instruction and makes the behavior undefined otherwise. A second instance of the same rule is also broken: the warpgroup does not synchronize between a partition's exit `setmaxnreg` and the dispatcher's next one. One option is a single adjustment per warpgroup on the dispatcher path; see Suggested fix.

#### Evidence

The partitions include the no-op padding partitions that `AllocateWarpGroups` adds, so a single 1-warp worker partition is enough to trigger this. For the mandatory `.aligned` qualifier, §9.7.21.5 allows `setmaxnreg` in conditional code only when every thread of the warpgroup evaluates the condition identically. Here the instructions have the same text but are distinct instructions, reached by a branch whose condition differs across the warpgroup.

**Example.** Tutorial `python/tutorials/gluon/08-warp-specialization.py`, `elementwise_add_warp_specialized_kernel`, compiled with Triton 3.8.0 for sm_90a, using the wrapper's default arguments:
- `XBLOCK=32`, `YBLOCK=64`;
- 2 load and 2 store buffers;
- `num_warps=4`, `maxnreg=128`;
- worker partitions `[1, 1]` warps with `[24, 24]` registers.

Warps 0–3 run the default partition. Warps 4–7 form one warpgroup holding the 2-warp padding partition, the load partition and the store partition. The default warps store the selector word `0x01000202` (line 127, before the barrier at 128), so warps 4–7 read 2, 2, 0, 1. Excerpt of the generated PTX, with line numbers from our file:

```
127:  st.shared.b32   [global_smem+49376], 16777730;   // selectors 2,2,0,1 for warps 4..7
...
314:  setmaxnreg.dec.sync.aligned.u32   24;           // all of warps 4..7
316:  ld.shared.b8    %r14, [%r16+49372];              // %r16 = global_smem + warp index
321-325:  $L_brx_0: .branchtargets $L__BB0_5, $L__BB0_9, $L__BB0_13, $L__BB0_18;   // selector 3 = exit
326:  brx.idx         %r14, $L_brx_0;
327: $L__BB0_5:                                        // selector 0: warp 6 (load)
328:  setmaxnreg.inc.sync.aligned.u32   24;
...
426: $L__BB0_9:                                        // selector 1: warp 7 (store)
427:  setmaxnreg.inc.sync.aligned.u32   24;
...
303: $L__BB0_13:                                       // selector 2: warps 4, 5 (padding)
305:  setmaxnreg.inc.sync.aligned.u32   24;
```

Warps 4 and 5 execute the instruction at 305, warp 6 the one at 328, and warp 7 the one at 427, all within one warpgroup. The exits differ the same way: 308 for warps 4 and 5, 424 for warp 6, and 522 for warp 7.

**The second instance.** PTX also requires all warps of the warpgroup to synchronize explicitly after a `setmaxnreg` before any of them executes the next one. Each partition's exit `setmaxnreg` branches straight back to the dispatcher's `setmaxnreg`, with no barrier in between: 424 → 314, 522 → 314 and 308 → 314. In the lowering, each `warp_return` becomes barrier, realloc, branch ([L420–L426](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/WarpSpecializeUtility.cpp#L420-L426)), and the switch loop starts with realloc, barrier ([L443–L445](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/WarpSpecializeUtility.cpp#L443-L445)). So warp 6 can execute 314 while warp 7 is still in the store partition.

**To reproduce.** On a Hopper GPU, run the tutorial's `test_elementwise_add_warp_specialized` with `num_warps=4`, then `grep -n setmaxnreg` the kernel's `.ptx` in the Triton cache.

#### Cause

The pattern comes from the lowering (permalinks at main `0d4e0a0`):
- `padToMaxWarpGroups` pads the worker partitions to whole warpgroups ([AllocateWarpGroups.cpp L39–L87](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/AllocateWarpGroups.cpp#L39-L87)). Every partition in a warpgroup then gets the same count, the warpgroup's maximum ([L220–L242](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/AllocateWarpGroups.cpp#L220-L242), [L265–L272](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/AllocateWarpGroups.cpp#L265-L272)).
- `rewritePartitionRegions` calls the target's `reallocRegisters` at the start of each partition region and at each `warp_return` ([WarpSpecializeUtility.cpp L391–L393](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/WarpSpecializeUtility.cpp#L391-L393), [L423–L425](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/lib/Conversion/TritonGPUToLLVM/WarpSpecializeUtility.cpp#L423-L425)). On NVIDIA, that emits a `setmaxnreg` ([ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM.cpp L231–L238](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/0d4e0a0ceae18cecacf582b9c6f557847a772bdf/third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/ConvertWarpSpecializeToLLVM.cpp#L231-L238)).

So partitions that share a warpgroup reach the same count through different instructions. The dispatcher chooses each warp's partition with a switch on a per-warp state byte; in the example above, that switch is a `brx.idx` jump table.

#### Suggested fix

Expected: every warp of a warpgroup executes the same `setmaxnreg` instruction, and the warpgroup synchronizes between consecutive ones. `AllocateWarpGroups` already gives each warpgroup a single count. One option is to emit each warpgroup's adjustment once, on the dispatcher path that all of its warps execute, rather than at each partition's entry and exit. #6694 notes that the per-partition instructions improved ptxas's registe

items.title: [FuseNestedLoops] flatten=True advances outer loop-carried indices on inner iterations
items.author: builtin-pb
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

**Summary.** With `tl.range(..., flatten=True)`, the kernel below returns wrong integers on Triton 3.5.1, 3.8.0 and main (`0d4e0a0c`): a value carried from two outer iterations back is combined with the index from one iteration back. `FuseNestedLoops::fuseOneLevel` delays the outer-yield update to the last inner iteration only for operands that are epilogue outputs, so prologue results and forwarded outer block arguments are updated on every inner iteration. Guarding every outer-yield operand fixes this case (diff below).

#### Reproduce

```python
import sys
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def flow_nested(X, Y, Z, Indices, Data, C, N, T, D, U, enabled,
                BLOCK: tl.constexpr, LOOP_STAGES: tl.constexpr,
                INNER_STAGES: tl.constexpr, FLATTEN: tl.constexpr,
                UNROLL: tl.constexpr, DISALLOW: tl.constexpr):
    pos = tl.program_id(0) * BLOCK + tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    valid = pos < N
    now = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    delayed_one = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    delayed_two = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    checksum = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    old_x = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    old_y = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    old_z = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    old_idx = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    old_valid = tl.full((BLOCK,), False, tl.int1)
    older_z = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    older_idx = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
    older_valid = tl.full((BLOCK,), False, tl.int1)
    for t in tl.range(0, T, num_stages=LOOP_STAGES, flatten=FLATTEN,
                      loop_unroll_factor=UNROLL, disallow_acc_multi_buffer=DISALLOW):
        if enabled and t % 3 != 1:
            g1 = tl.load(Data + pos * D + old_idx,
                         old_valid & (old_idx >= 0) & (old_idx < D), other=0).to(tl.int32)
            delayed_one += tl.where(old_valid, (old_x * old_y + g1) * (t + 1), 0)
        if enabled and t % 2 == 0:
            g2 = tl.load(Data + pos * D + older_idx,
                         older_valid & (older_idx >= 0) & (older_idx < D), other=0).to(tl.int32)
            delayed_two += tl.where(older_valid, (2 * older_z + g2) * (t + 1), 0)
        x = tl.load(X + t * N + pos, valid, other=0).to(tl.int32)
        y = tl.load(Y + t * N + pos, valid, other=0).to(tl.int32)
        z = tl.load(Z + t * N + pos, valid, other=0).to(tl.int32)
        idx = tl.load(Indices + t * N + pos, valid, other=0)
        now += x * y + z * (t + 1)
        checksum += y * (pos + 1) + idx * (t + 1)
        inner_old = tl.zeros((BLOCK,), tl.int32)
        inner_valid = tl.full((BLOCK,), False, tl.int1)
        for s in tl.range(0, U, num_stages=INNER_STAGES, flatten=FLATTEN,
                          loop_unroll_factor=UNROLL, disallow_acc_multi_buffer=DISALLOW):
            neighbor = (pos + s + 1) % N
            inner_z = tl.load(Z + t * N + neighbor, valid, other=0).to(tl.int32)
            if enabled and (t + s) % 2 == 0:
                checksum += (inner_z + x * (s + 1)) * (t + 1) * (s + 1)
            if enabled and s % 2 == 1:
                checksum += tl.where(inner_valid, inner_old * (s + 1), 0)
            inner_old = inner_z
            inner_valid = valid
        older_z = old_z
        older_idx = old_idx
        older_valid = old_valid
        old_x = x
        old_y = y
        old_z = z
        old_idx = idx
        old_valid = valid
    tl.store(C + 4 * pos, now, valid)
    tl.store(C + 4 * pos + 1, delayed_one, valid)
    tl.store(C + 4 * pos + 2, delayed_two, valid)
    tl.store(C + 4 * pos + 3, checksum, valid)


def reference(X, Y, Z, I, Data, N, T, D, U):
    out = []
    for p in range(N):
        now = d1 = d2 = ck = 0
        old = older = None  # (x, y, z, idx) of the previous / second-previous outer iteration
        for t in range(T):
            if t % 3 != 1 and old:
                d1 += (old[0] * old[1] + Data[p * D + old[3]]) * (t + 1)
            if t % 2 == 0 and older:
                d2 += (2 * older[2] + Data[p * D + older[3]]) * (t + 1)
            x, y, z, idx = X[t * N + p], Y[t * N + p], Z[t * N + p], I[t * N + p]
            now += x * y + z * (t + 1)
            ck += y * (p + 1) + idx * (t + 1)
            inner_old = None
            for s in range(U):
                inner_z = Z[t * N + (p + s + 1) % N]
                if (t + s) % 2 == 0:
                    ck += (inner_z + x * (s + 1)) * (t + 1) * (s + 1)
                if s % 2 == 1 and inner_old is not None:
                    ck += inner_old * (s + 1)
                inner_old = inner_z
            older, old = old, (x, y, z, idx)
        out += [now, d1, d2, ck]
    return out


def main():
    print("torch", torch.__version__, "triton", triton.__version__, torch.cuda.get_device_name())
    g = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
    D, bad = 7, 0
    for flatten in (False, True):
        for N, T, U in ((129, 3, 2), (129, 4, 3), (256, 3, 2), (300, 5, 2), (64, 6, 3)):
            X, Y, Z = (torch.randint(-3, 4, (T * N,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int8) for _ in range(3))
            I = torch.randint(0, D, (T * N,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int32)
            Data = torch.randint(-3, 4, (N * D,), generator=g, dtype=torch.int8)
            C = torch.zeros(4 * N, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
            flow_nested[(triton.cdiv(N, 256),)](X.cuda(), Y.cuda(), Z.cuda(), I.cuda(), Data.cuda(), C, N, T, D, U, True,
                                                BLOCK=256, LOOP_STAGES=2, INNER_STAGES=3, FLATTEN=flatten,
                                                UNROLL=1, DISALLOW=False, num_warps=1, num_stages=2)
            want = reference(X.tolist(), Y.tolist(), Z.tolist(), I.tolist(), Data.tolist(), N, T, D, U)
            got = C.tolist()
            diff = [k for k in range(4 * N) if got[k] != want[k]]
            bad += bool(diff)
            first = f" first: element {diff[0]} (lane {diff[0] // 4}, output {diff[0] % 4}) got {got[diff[0]]} want {want[diff[0]]}" if

items.title: Autotuner memoizes incorrectly on mixed-architecture setups
items.author: turboderp
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`Autotuner.cache` is keyed only on key-arg values and dtypes. So a process using one decorated kernel on two devices of different capability uses the config from whichever device ran first, even if the second device is incompatible. `_bench()` drops configs that raise `OutOfResources`, but only on the device that ran the benchmark.

Miminal example is one kernel with two configs, where one config needs >64 kB smem, run on an Ampere GPU and then on a Turing GPU; nothing causes the autotuner to treat the two GPUs differently, so the second launch fails if autotuning picked the >64 kB config.

As far as I can tell it's fixable in [`Autotuner.run()`](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/3078daa76bbd55c1c3509f7ee8e899b1ed6a127e/python/triton/runtime/autotuner.py#L238) by appending e.g. `driver.active.get_current_target()` to the key, mirroring what the JIT compile cache already does.

### Environment details

Triton: Latest
GPU: Mixed setups

items.title: `ptr - x` with an unsigned offset moves the pointer forward by 2^k - x
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

`ptr - x` with an unsigned offset `x` narrower than 64 bits moves the pointer forward instead of backward. The compiled kernel and the interpreter both read the wrong addresses; with `uint32` the address is about 2^32 elements past the pointer.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(X, Y):
    i = tl.arange(0, 64)
    tl.store(Y + i, tl.load(X + 300 - i.to(tl.uint8)))  # X[300 - i]


x = torch.arange(1024, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float32)
y = torch.empty(64, device="cuda")
kernel[(1, )](x, y)
print(y[:5].tolist())
```

```
[300.0, 555.0, 554.0, 553.0, 552.0]
```

Expected `[300.0, 299.0, 298.0, 297.0, 296.0]`. The kernel reads `X[300 + 256 - i]`.

`semantic.sub` lowers `ptr - x` as `add(ptr, minus(x))`. `minus` computes `0 - x` in `x`'s unsigned type, which wraps to `2^k - x`, and `add` then zero-extends unsigned offsets to int64 (#5373), so the pointer moves by `+(2^k - x)`. `ptr + x` with an unsigned `x` is correct since #5373; only the subtraction is affected. Signed offsets and `uint64` are correct.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8. The bug is in the frontend; `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` reads the same wrong addresses.

items.title: Casting between fp8e5 and fp8e4nv fails to compile: "Rounding mode must be specified for convertsions to fp8"
items.author: shuyilinn
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Casting between the two fp8 formats (`float8e5` to `float8e4nv` and back) fails to compile on sm_89: the NVIDIA lowering hits an assertion (in a source build with assertions enabled). There is no workaround: `fp_downcast_rounding` is rejected for this cast. The interpreter accepts the cast.

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def cast(X, Y):
    offs = tl.arange(0, 16)
    tl.store(Y + offs, tl.load(X + offs).to(Y.dtype.element_ty))


x = torch.full((16, ), 1.5, device="cuda").to(torch.float8_e5m2)
y = torch.zeros(16, device="cuda", dtype=torch.float8_e4m3fn)
cast[(1, )](x, y)
print(y.float()[0].item())
```

```
ElementwiseOpToLLVM.cpp:425: ... FpToFpOpConversion::createDestOps(...): Assertion `roundingMode.has_value() && "Rounding mode must be specified for convertsions to fp8"' failed.
...
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed
```

Expected `1.5`.

`cast` in `python/triton/language/semantic.py` sets a default rounding mode only for casts to a narrower type, and raises if `fp_downcast_rounding` is passed for any other cast. The fp8 to fp8 `tt.fp_to_fp` therefore has no rounding mode, and `FpToFpOpConversion` (`third_party/nvidia/lib/TritonNVIDIAGPUToLLVM/ElementwiseOpToLLVM.cpp`) asserts that conversions to fp8 have one. Both directions can lose information (e5m2 to e4m3 can overflow, e4m3 to e5m2 drops a mantissa bit), so the cast does need a rounding mode.

### Environment details

Triton: main @ 41846bc965
GPU: NVIDIA RTX 4090 (sm_89), driver 570 / CUDA 12.8
Build: from source, with assertions enabled

items.title: [Performance] Dot-operand conversion hoisting replicates integer metadata packing
items.author: IlyasMoutawwakil
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the issue

While optimizing a BF16 × INT4 weight-only GEMM, I found that dot-operand layout-conversion hoisting moves compact integer metadata packing into a layout that replicates the arithmetic. Keeping the packing before the transfer is faster in this workload, provided the transfer is also scheduled before the large MMA operand loads.

This is a performance issue; outputs are correct. The measured gain from an experimental compiler change is small (~1.4%), but the layout/scheduling interaction seemed worth reporting.

### Standalone pass reproducer

Save the following as `repro.py` and run `python repro.py`. It only needs Triton; no Torch, GPU, project package, or checkpoint is needed. This reproduces the pass transformation, **not the full GEMM timing**. Both halves of the packed metadata are consumed and the result feeds the dot operand.

```python
import tempfile
from pathlib import Path
import triton
from triton._C.libtriton import ir, passes, nvidia

CASE = r"""
// RUN: triton-opt %s -tritongpu-remove-layout-conversions -cse
#load = #ttg.blocked<{sizePerThread = [1, 2], threadsPerWarp = [16, 2], warpsPerCTA = [2, 1], order = [1, 0]}>
#expanded = #ttg.linear<{register = [[0, 0, 1], [0, 0, 2], [0, 0, 4], [8, 0, 0], [0, 0, 32], [0, 0, 64], [0, 1, 0], [0, 2, 0]], lane = [[0, 0, 8], [0, 0, 16], [1, 0, 0], [2, 0, 0], [4, 0, 0]], warp = [[16, 0, 0]], block = []}>
#meta = #ttg.slice<{dim = 2, parent = #expanded}>
#mma = #ttg.nvidia_mma<{versionMajor = 2, versionMinor = 0, warpsPerCTA = [2, 1], instrShape = [16, 8]}>
#dot0 = #ttg.dot_op<{opIdx = 0, parent = #mma, kWidth = 8}>
#dot1 = #ttg.dot_op<{opIdx = 1, parent = #mma, kWidth = 8}>
module attributes {"ttg.num-ctas" = 1 : i32, "ttg.num-warps" = 2 : i32, "ttg.threads-per-warp" = 32 : i32} {
  tt.func @replicated_integer_metadata(%zp: tensor<32x4x!tt.ptr<i8>, #load>, %a: tensor<512x2xbf16, #dot1>, %weights: tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>, %acc: tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>) -> tensor<32x2xf32, #mma> {
    %magic = arith.constant dense<49920> : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %dup = arith.constant dense<65537> : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %z = tt.load %zp : tensor<32x4x!tt.ptr<i8>, #load>
    %wide = arith.extui %z : tensor<32x4xi8, #load> to tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %lifted = arith.ori %wide, %magic : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %packed = arith.muli %lifted, %dup : tensor<32x4xi32, #load>
    %converted = ttg.convert_layout %packed : tensor<32x4xi32, #load> -> tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %pairs = tt.elementwise_inline_asm "add.rn.bf16x2 $0, $1, $2;" {constraints = "=r,r,r", packed_element = 1 : i32, pure = true} %weights, %converted : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>, tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %shift = arith.constant dense<16> : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %hi32 = arith.shrui %pairs, %shift : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta>
    %hi16 = arith.trunci %hi32 : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> to tensor<32x4xi16, #meta>
    %hibf = tt.bitcast %hi16 : tensor<32x4xi16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %lo = arith.trunci %pairs : tensor<32x4xi32, #meta> to tensor<32x4xi16, #meta>
    %bf = tt.bitcast %lo : tensor<32x4xi16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %sum = arith.addf %bf, %hibf : tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta>
    %ex = tt.expand_dims %sum {axis = 2 : i32} : tensor<32x4xbf16, #meta> -> tensor<32x4x1xbf16, #expanded>
    %bc = tt.broadcast %ex : tensor<32x4x1xbf16, #expanded> -> tensor<32x4x128xbf16, #expanded>
    %lhs = tt.reshape %bc : tensor<32x4x128xbf16, #expanded> -> tensor<32x512xbf16, #dot0>
    %out = tt.dot %lhs, %a, %acc, inputPrecision = tf32 : tensor<32x512xbf16, #dot0> * tensor<512x2xbf16, #dot1> -> tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>
    tt.return %out : tensor<32x2xf32, #mma>
  }
}
"""

print("Triton:", triton.__version__)
ctx = ir.context()
ir.load_dialects(ctx)
nvidia.load_dialects(ctx)
with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as directory:
    source = Path(directory) / "repro.mlir"
    source.write_text(CASE)
    module = ir.parse_mlir_module(str(source), ctx)
    pm = ir.pass_manager(ctx)
    passes.ttgpuir.add_remove_layout_conversions(pm)
    passes.common.add_cse(pm)
    pm.run(module, "repro")
    print(module)
```

Alternatively, the `CASE` string can be saved as `repro.mlir` and run with:

```sh
triton-opt repro.mlir -tritongpu-remove-layout-conversions -cse
```

On stock v3.8.0, the relevant output order is:

```text
load i8 in producer layout
convert_layout i8 to replicated layout
extui
ori
muli
... packed BF16 arithmetic and dot ...
```

The producer has two unique metadata elements per thread; the destination slice layout has eight. The packing arithmetic therefore runs on four times as many elements per thread. The input IR already places the i32 packing before its conversion, but the pass hoists the conversion above it.

Could `hoistConvertDotOperand` account for this replication cost while preserving weight-load pipelining? The ordinary rematerialization path already has `getCostFactor`/`isRematBeneficial`, whereas this hoisting path walks through pure elementwise operations to the loads without that profitability check:

- [v3.8.0 implementation](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/c01b6774b1865984607d89d89d3a10833de92037/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp#L1237)
- [Current main implementation inspected](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/lib/Dialect/TritonGPU/Transforms/RemoveLayoutConversions.cpp#L1227)

### Full-workload observations

The originating workload is a dense weight-only GEMM: M=2, N=12288, K=4096; BF16 activations/scales; asymmetric INT4 weights; UINT8 zero points; group size 128. Frozen configuration: BM2/BN32/BK512, pointer loads, transposed operand orientation, two warps, three stages, split-K 1. It uses packed BF16 dequantization with the scale-dtype rounding preserved.

Seven alternating CUDA-graph measurements of the same public wrapper and identical weights/configuration:

| | Stock v3.8.0 | Experimental compiler

items.title: A `for` loop silently widens a bound or step with the loop variable's signedness instead of its own
items.author: Hughshine
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug


**TL;DR.** `for i in range(lb, ub, step)` promotes the types of `lb`, `ub` and `step` to one type, which becomes the type of the loop variable `i` (`int32` for `range(n)`), and casts each operand to it. When an operand is narrower, the cast chooses sign or zero extension by whether the loop variable's type is signed, instead of whether the operand's type is, so it is wrong whenever the two differ: an unsigned operand (`uint8`, `uint16`, `bool`) in a signed loop is sign-extended, and a signed operand in an unsigned loop is zero-extended. `range(n)` with a `uint8` `n` of 200 runs 0 iterations. Not a regression. Possible fix: extend each operand by its own signedness, as `tl.cast` does.

A kernel that loops over a count read from a `uint8` tensor is enough (the control differs only in an explicit `.to(tl.int32)` of the bound):

```python
import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def count(n_ptr, out_ptr, CAST: tl.constexpr):
    n = tl.load(n_ptr)  # uint8 scalar
    if CAST:
        n = n.to(tl.int32)  # control: the same bound as int32
    c = 0
    for i in range(n):
        c += 1
    tl.store(out_ptr, c)


n = torch.tensor([200], dtype=torch.uint8, device="cuda")
for cast in (True, False):
    out = torch.zeros(1, dtype=torch.int32, device="cuda")
    count[(1, )](n, out, cast)
    print(f"CAST={cast!s:5} iterations: {out.item()}, expected {n.item()}")
```

Observed on main @2122e24ef:
```
CAST=True  iterations: 200, expected 200
CAST=False iterations: 0, expected 200
```
Expected: 200 in both. Loops in a kernel follow Python's `range` (the `tl.range` docstring: ["similar semantics to Python's `range`"](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/language/core.py#L3663-L3664)), the control gives 200, and `TRITON_INTERPRET=1` gives 200 for both. In the TTIR the explicit cast is an `arith.extui` and the loop's own widening an `arith.extsi`, so the byte 200 becomes -56:
```
CAST=True : %n_0 = arith.extui %n : i8 to i32
CAST=False: %0 = arith.extsi %n : i8 to i32
```

**How the bounds are converted.** `visit_For` does two things:
1. It promotes the three operand types to one type, the type of the loop variable `i` (below: the loop type) ([code_generator.py#L1349-L1350](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1349-L1350)): the wider type wins, and at equal width the unsigned one. The defaults `lb = 0` and `step = 1` are `int32` ([L1325-L1327](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1325-L1327)), so `range(n)` and `range(lb, ub)` loop over `int32` unless an operand is `int64`, `uint32` or `uint64`.
2. It casts each operand to that type with one signedness flag for all three, taken from the loop type ([L1352-L1360](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/compiler/code_generator.py#L1352-L1360)). `create_int_cast` emits `arith.bitcast` at equal width and, when widening, `arith.extsi` if the flag is set and `arith.extui` otherwise ([ir.cc#L1331-L1340](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/src/ir.cc#L1331-L1340)).

Whether a widening keeps the value depends on the operand's type, not the loop's, so two of the four widening cases are wrong (`range(lb, ub)` with loaded scalars, L40S):

| operand to loop type | example | operand becomes | should become | main @2122e24ef | with the change |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| signed to signed | `lb` int8 -5, `ub` int32 10 | -5 (`extsi`) | -5 | 15 iterations from -5 | same |
| unsigned to unsigned | `lb` uint32 0, `ub` uint8 200 | 200 (`extui`) | 200 | 200 iterations | same |
| **unsigned to signed** | `lb` int32 0, `ub` uint8 200 | **-56** (`extsi`) | 200 | **0 iterations** | 200 |
| **signed to unsigned** | `lb` int8 -5, `ub` uint32 300 | **251** (`extui`) | 4294967291 | **49 iterations from 251** | 305 from 4294967291 |
| equal width | `lb` int32 -5, `ub` uint32 300 | 4294967291 (`bitcast`) | 4294967291 | 305 from 4294967291 | same |

The last row is the existing behaviour for an equal-width mix, and it is also what `tl.cast` gives, since `tl.cast` extends by the source type's signedness ([semantic.py#L912](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/language/semantic.py#L909-L912)); with the change the signed-to-unsigned row agrees with it. A `bool` is `int1` ([semantic.py#L140-L141](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/language/semantic.py#L140-L141)), which is listed with the unsigned types ([core.py#L403](https://github.com/triton-lang/triton/blob/2122e24efc1886bfa36337c1f5b07c47d827b1d4/python/triton/language/core.py#L403)), so `True` becomes -1. Workaround: convert the operand to the loop type before the loop (the control above).

<details>
<summary>More unsigned-to-signed loops, sources, versions and the differential test</summary>

Only operands with the top bit set are affected: `uint8` 128 to 255, `uint16` 32768 to 65535, `bool` True. Measured on an L40S, main @2122e24ef, loaded scalars unless noted:

| loop | main @2122e24ef | with the change |
|---|---|---|
| `range(lb, 300)`, `lb` uint8 200 | 356 iterations, `i` from -56 | 100, from 200 |
| `range(0, 1000, s)`, `s` uint8 200 | 38347923 iterations | 5 |
| `range(n)`, `n` uint16 40000 | 0 iterations | 40000 |
| `range(n)`, `n` bool True | 0 iterations | 1 |
| `range(flag, 4)`, `flag` a `tl.constexpr` True | 5 iterations, `i` from -1 | 3, from 1 |
| `range(lb, ub)`, uint8 125 and 131 | 0 iterations | 6 |
| `range(lb, ub)`, uint8 133 and 138 | 5 iterations, `i` = -123 to -119 | 5, `i` = 133 to 137 |
| the same loop summing `tl.load(x_ptr + i)` over `x = arange(256)` | reads 5 elements before `x` (nan he

items.author: Jeffwan
items.body_excerpt:
### 🚀 Feature Description and Motivation

low priority since context-first mode has been supported

The pd router currently only supports context-first scheduling (sequential: prefill → wait for response → decode). 

TRT-LLM also supports generation-first mode where the proxy sends context_only and generation_only requests in parallel — the GEN worker enters `DISAGG_GENERATION_INIT` state, uses ctx_info_endpoint + disagg_request_id to pull KV cache directly from the CTX worker while it's still computing, reducing end-to-end  latency. 

Implementation requires: caching `/server_info` from CTX workers at router init (returns ctx_info_endpoint and ctx_dp_rank), dispatching both requests concurrently via goroutines, injecting the cached server info into  the GEN request's disaggregated_params, and setting schedule_style: 

> Note that ctx_dp_rank is the attention data-parallel rank — relevant when CTX workers use data parallelism (TP x DP). For single-instance  deployments it's 0, but for multi-instance setups the router needs to track which DP rank each CTX worker exposes and match correctly when routing.


### Use Case

Support generation-first strategy

items.title: [Feat] Track remaining SGLang DP-attention metric aggregation and mapping gaps
items.author: MuonChaser
items.body_excerpt:
### Feature Description and Motivation

Track the remaining SGLang DP-attention metric aggregation work identified in the [review of #3156](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/pull/3156#pullrequestreview-5563897481).

#3156 addresses the four request/KV pool gauges reported in #3155: running requests, queued requests, KV capacity and capacity-weighted token utilization. It deliberately leaves other families unchanged. This follow-up is separate from that fix and is not intended to block it.

AIBrix also maps the following SGLang gauges in [`pkg/metrics/metrics.go`](https://github.com/vllm-project/aibrix/blob/c31f4e07d5170003359387fa2cd46fe588803332/pkg/metrics/metrics.go):

| AIBrix metric | SGLang mapping | Follow-up |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `AvgGenerationThroughputToksPerS` | `sglang:gen_throughput` | Prioritize validating pod-level aggregation of independent DP throughput |
| `NumRequestsSwapped` | `sglang:num_retracted_reqs` | Verify the legacy gauge's update semantics and whether this mapping remains appropriate |
| `NumPrefillPreallocQueueReqs` | `sglang:num_prefill_prealloc_queue_reqs` | Verify name/version compatibility before defining aggregation |
| `NumDecodePreallocQueueReqs` | `sglang:num_decode_prealloc_queue_reqs` | Verify DP ownership and priority/total series before aggregation |

### Use Case and Current Evidence

When one endpoint exposes multiple independent DP pools, consuming one rank can understate pod-level throughput or queue pressure. Replicated TP/PP/EP observations must not be counted as additional pools.

The current follow-up evidence is code inspection and synthetic regression coverage, not a new live reproduction of all four metrics:

- `TestSGLangDPPriorityScopesAndLegacy` in #3156 deliberately retains two `sglang:gen_throughput` series (10 and 20) unchanged. The typed-read selection paths still select one series per model rather than sum those DP pools. If the two values represent independent DP generation rates, the desired pod-level value is 30, not 10 or 20.
- [SGLang v0.5.21's collector](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/blob/v0.5.21/python/sglang/srt/observability/metrics_collector.py) defines `gen_throughput` as generation token/s. It also marks `num_retracted_reqs` as an old gauge with a newer counter available.
- That collector defines `num_prefill_bootstrap_queue_reqs` and `num_prefill_inflight_queue_reqs`, rather than AIBrix's mapped `num_prefill_prealloc_queue_reqs`. The decode preallocation gauge is present. Compatibility needs investigation; simply extending the aggregation allowlist would not resolve a missing metric name.
- The real GPU scrape/replay evidence attached to #3156 validates its four targeted request/KV gauges. It does not establish correct aggregation semantics for the additional metrics listed here.

### Proposed Solution and Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Start with generation throughput: capture representative DP-attention scrapes and verify that the reported rank values describe independent generation work and compatible measurement windows.
- [ ] Document each additional metric's supported SGLang versions, labels, update semantics, and aggregation policy. Identify deprecated or renamed mappings separately.
- [ ] Aggregate only verified additive quantities across distinct DP pools, deduplicating replicated TP/PP/EP observations. Preserve model, engine-role, extra-label and priority scopes; never add a priority total to its breakdowns.
- [ ] Add local HTTP fetcher regressions covering both `FetchAllTypedMetrics` and `FetchTypedMetric`, exposition-order independence, replicated ranks, separate scopes and legacy unranked input.
- [ ] Validate prefill/decode queue behavior in the applicable PD configuration before claiming coverage. Leave unsupported or ambiguous metrics unchanged and document the limitation.

Related: #3155 and #3156 (targeted fix); #1614 (broader utilization/load reporting); #3056/#3057 (priority-series selection, a separate concern).

### Environment

Scope reviewed against AIBrix PR #3156 head `c31f4e07d5170003359387fa2cd46fe588803332` and SGLang v0.5.21. No Kubernetes end-to-end validation or measured routing/autoscaling improvement is claimed for this follow-up.

### Area

Gateway

items.title: Assertion in TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers: "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" on a pointer select inside a runtime scf.if
items.author: O1iveira7
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

Compiling a legal Triton kernel fails with a C++ assertion in the AMD `TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` pass. The kernel merges two pointer bases with `tl.where` under a tensor condition inside a runtime `if`; the pass then hits a mixed representation between the two `scf.if` arms and aborts compilation.


**Error log**
```
CanonicalizePointers.cpp:1445: ... ConvertSCFIfOp::matchAndRewrite_(scf::IfOp, OneToNOpAdaptor, ...):
Assertion ifOp.thenYield()->hasAttr(kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets) &&
          "expected then yield to report fat ptr indices" failed.
note: Pipeline failed while executing [TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers` on 'tt.func' operation: @kernel]
RuntimeError: PassManager::run failed

Failure is in `make_ttgir` (MLIR), before LLVM codegen; exit code 1.
```

The generated TTGIR is:

```
%5 = scf.if %4 -> (tensor<2x!tt.ptr<f32>>) {
  %11 = tt.addptr %10, %0          // base = splat(arg1)
  %12 = arith.select %9, %11, %2   // tensor condition, different bases
  scf.yield %12
} else {
  scf.yield %2                     // base = splat(arg2)
}
%8 = tt.load %5
```
TritonAMDGPUCanonicalizePointers is a 1:N conversion to fat pointers (scalar base, tensor offset). scf.if is only rewritten after both scf.yields are rewritten (tracked via internal then/else-rewritten attributes). ConvertSCFYieldOp sets kSCFIfOpYieldFatPtrOffsets on a yield only when one of its remapped operands is a 2-element fat pointer, while ConvertSCFIfOp unconditionally asserts that the then-yield has that attribute.

Here ConvertArithSelectOp takes its special case for a tensor condition with differing scalar bases and materializes both arms into full tensor pointers instead of a (base, offset) pair. So the then-yield carries a single materialized pointer and gets no fat-pointer index attribute, while the else-yield (a plain tt.addptr) converts to a fat pointer pair and does get the attribute. Both yields are marked rewritten, the scf.if becomes illegal, ConvertSCFIfOp fires, and the assertion fails on the inconsistent arms.

**Reproducer**
```
import os

import torch
import triton
import triton.language as tl


@triton.jit
def kernel(sw, a_ptr, b_ptr, BLOCK: tl.constexpr):
    offs = tl.arange(0, BLOCK)
    p = b_ptr + offs
    if tl.load(sw) == 0:
        p = tl.where(offs >= 0, a_ptr + offs, b_ptr + offs)
    tl.store(a_ptr + offs, tl.load(p))


def _main() -> None:
    device = "cuda"
    N = 2
    a = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    b = torch.randn(N, device=device)
    sw = torch.tensor([0], dtype=torch.int32, device=device)
    print(f"REPRO_START N={N} buffer_ops={os.environ.get('AMDGCN_USE_BUFFER_OPS', 'default')}", flush=True)
    kernel[(1,)](sw, a, b, BLOCK=N, num_warps=1)
    torch.cuda.synchronize()
    print("REPRO_DONE (no crash)", flush=True)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    _main()
```

### Environment details

- AMD Instinct MI308X (gfx942), ROCm 7.2.3
- triton-rocm 3.8.0, torch 2.14.0+rocm7.2, Python 3.12.13

comments.author: he-yufeng
comments.body:
Picking this up; the earlier attempt #12182 is closed unmerged and the assert is still in place on current main (2a514c0f).

The mechanism in the report checks out. The trigger is the tensor-condition case of ConvertArithSelectOp: with different scalar bases it materializes both arms into full tensor pointers, so the then yield carries one plain pointer and ConvertSCFYieldOp records no fat-ptr offsets for it, while the else yield still carries a (base, offset) pair and does get the attribute. Once both yields are marked rewritten, ConvertSCFIfOp fires and asserts on the asymmetry. Reproduced locally with triton-opt on an asserts-enabled build, same assert as the report (CanonicalizePointers.cpp:1450).

That asymmetric shape is legal output of the select conversion, and downstream consumers already accept a materialized pointer (MaterializeFatPointer passes through any pointer operand that does not arrive as a pair), so the natural place for the fix is the scf.if boundary: for each result where the two yields disagree on the representation, materialize the (base, offset) side into a tensor pointer before rebuilding the op. Results that stay fat on both sides keep the pair form and the existing attribute propagation. The same hole exists when both arms materialize (neither yield reports offsets and the old code asserts on the then yield all the same); the fix covers that shape too.

PR coming with lit coverage for both. No AMD hardware here, so verification is at the MLIR level only.

items.title: SM120: sparse_mla_sm120_prefill illegal memory access (Xid 31) on DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash long prefill — persists in 0.7.0 (#4802); deterministic when CUDA graphs enabled
items.author: Lei-010
items.body_excerpt:
### Describe the bug

On **SM120 (RTX PRO 6000, sm_120)**, `sparse_mla_sm120_prefill` triggers an **illegal memory access (Xid 31, MMU Fault: FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ)** on all 4 GPUs simultaneously during **long prefill (>35K tokens)** with DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (sparse MLA + Engram compressed KV).

This **persists in FlashInfer 0.7.0** (tested the `sm120f` jit-cache build + cubin + cu130 x86_64 wheels): #4802 (SM120 sparse MLA refactor) and #5048 (SM120 prefill hang fix) do **not** cover this shape. Short sequences pass; a single 35K-token prefill is enough to fault.

### Key finding: CUDA graphs make it deterministic

| Config | Short seq | Long prefill (35K+) |
|---|---|---|
| eager / compile-only (graph dispatched off) | ✅ pass | 2 crashes / 6 passes (~25%, flaky) |
| CUDA graphs = FULL / FULL_DECODE_ONLY / PIECEWISE | ✅ pass | **0/3 — faults on the FIRST 35K prefill** |

Any graph mode — even decode-only capture — makes the long-prefill fault 100% reproducible. With graphs off the fault is intermittent on identical inputs. This points at an **allocator/address-layout interaction**: graph capture reserves padded KV pools, and the compressed-layer page geometry (block-size 64) then produces an out-of-range page-table entry during long-prefill sparse gather.

### Environment

- 4× NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), driver 580.x, CUDA 13.0
- vLLM v0.30.0 + FlashInfer 0.6.18.post1 → 0.7.0 (both affected)
- `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_DSV41` backend, `indexer_kv_dtype=fp8`, `--block-size 64`, TP=4
- Model: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash (43 layers, compress_ratios [0,0,2x18,1x20,0,0,0])

### Xid sample

```
NVRM: Xid (PCI:0000:16:00): 31, name=VLLM::Worker, MMU Fault: ENGINE GRAPHICS GPC*, faulted @ 0x7f..., Fault is of type FAULT_PDE ACCESS_TYPE_VIRT_READ
```

### Related

- Full vLLM-side report + reproduction steps: vllm-project/vllm#58910
- #4973 — same Xid signature on SM120 + RTX PRO 6000 (short OK / long prefill fault); the reported B12X workaround does not apply here (model code hard-selects the sparse path)

We can provide the full crash matrix, dmesg captures, and a 100%-reproducible graph-mode sequence.

comments.author: Lei-010
comments.body:
### Retest on vLLM + FlashInfer 0.7.1rc5: 3/3 long prefills pass, zero Xid 31

Following @adi-suresh01's pointer in vllm-project/vllm#58910 — retested the long-prefill fault on the same class of hardware that produced the original report (this issue was filed from our box on 2026-09-27 against FlashInfer 0.7.0).

**Verdict: the fault no longer reproduces on 0.7.1rc5**, under the exact condition that made it deterministic before (CUDA graphs enabled).

#### Stack under test

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Hardware | 8 × RTX PRO 6000 (SM120, 96 GB), TP8 |
| FlashInfer | **0.7.1rc5** (`flashinfer_python-0.7.1rc5.dist-info`, cu130 wheels; files dated 2026-10-11) |
| Confirmed #5197 code present | `flashinfer/mla/_sparse_mla_sm120/` package; `dsv41_fp4_quantize_pack_sparse_mla_cache` and `dsv41_fp4_quantize_append_sparse_mla_cache` exported |
| Model | DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, `max_model_len` 1,048,576 |
| Graphs | `--max-cudagraph-capture-size 512`, compilation-config default (PIECEWISE) — i.e. graphs **on** |
| KV | `--kv-cache-dtype fp8`, `--block-size 64`, `kv_cache_size_tokens` 3,806,086 (`num_gpu_blocks` 100,501), prefix caching **on** |
| Spec decode | DSpark, `num_speculative_tokens 3` |
| Other | `--gpu-memory-utilization 0.93`, `--reasoning-parser deepseek_v41` |

The prior report's table showed *0/3 passes* on the first 35K prefill whenever CUDA graphs were FULL / FULL_DECODE_ONLY / PIECEWISE. That setting is unchanged here, so this is not a "graphs got turned off" pass.

#### Test

Three sequential single-request prefills, non-streaming, `temperature 0`, `max_tokens 32`. Each request carried a unique nonce prefix so prefix caching could not turn the prefill into a cache hit.

```
run1: OK   3.08 s   prompt_tokens=44963   completion=32
run2: OK   3.10 s   prompt_tokens=44963   completion=32
run3: OK   3.07 s   prompt_tokens=44963   completion=32
```

44,963 tokens is above the >35K threshold that faulted before. All three completed with HTTP 200 and no degraded output.

#### Fault indicators

| Check | Before run | After run |
|---|---|---|
| `dmesg` Xid count | 0 | **0** |
| Container log: `Xid` / `illegal memory` / `device-side assert` | none | **none** |

The Xid counter is per-boot; the host had been up ~7 days at test time, so this covers the whole uptime including routine traffic, not just the three requests.

#### Scope / what this does not establish

- **Single-request only.** No concurrency sweep; the original report was also single-request, so this is an apples-to-apples retest of the fault, not a throughput claim.
- Prefill latency above is single-stream, prefix-cache-cold, and includes no queueing (one request in flight at a time).
- The dmesg counter cannot distinguish "this shape never faults" from "this shape faults below the rate we sampled" — 3 runs is a smoke-level confirmation, not a probabilistic bound. If the original ~25 % eager-mode flakiness is still latent somewhere, 3 clean runs would not rule it out; it does rule out the previous deterministic-with-graphs behaviour.
- We did not bisect #5197 against 0.7.0 on this box; the conclusion is only that 0.7.1rc5 is clean here.

Happy to run a larger N or a concurrency tier if that would help close it out.

comments.author: adi-suresh01
comments.body:
Thanks for the retest. A data point for the longer end of your scope note: on 4x RTX PRO 6000 Server Edition (TP4, PCIe only, driver 595.91.07), vLLM nightly `49cb2bbf` with FlashInfer 0.7.2 plus vllm-project/vllm#60762's 64-token blocks served single 10.7K, 31K and 106K-token prefills with CUDA graphs on and no speculation, and 10.7K and 106K with DSpark (k=5), with no fault: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/56771#issuecomment-6227106955

With your 3/3 at 45K on 0.7.1rc5, this issue and vllm-project/vllm#58910 look ready to close.

comments.author: Lei-010
comments.body:
Thanks — that closes the last gap I cared about. Your 106K-token run on 0.7.2 with DSpark k=5 covers the exact combination my scope note flagged as untested (long *and* speculative), so between your data point and our 3 × 44,963 on 0.7.1rc5 there is no configuration left where the prefill fault reproduces.

Two notes for whoever closes this, from our side:

1. We have **not** moved off 0.7.1rc5 yet — production is still on the 0.7.1rc5 wheel and we plan to hold there for a few days before bumping to 0.7.2, so if anything regresses on 0.7.2 we will report it here rather than silently.
2. One thing that is worth recording so it is not lost: the DSpark draft head still logs `does not support external multimodal embeddings` on our TP8 box. That is orthogonal to this issue and does not affect correctness, but it is a warning people will keep hitting while spec decoding + images are both enabled.

No objection to closing #5608 and vllm#58910 from our side.

items.title: Feature Request: Graceful reasoning budget termination. Avoid mid-sentence cutoff.
items.author: CleStil
items.body_excerpt:
### Prerequisites

- [x] I am running the latest code. Mention the version if possible as well.
- [x] I carefully followed the [README.md](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/README.md).
- [x] I searched using keywords relevant to my issue to make sure that I am creating a new issue that is not already open (or closed).
- [x] I reviewed the [Discussions](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/discussions), and have a new and useful enhancement to share.

### Feature Description

PR #20297 (merged ~2025-03-11) added `--reasoning-budget-message`, which injects
a string at the hard token cutoff to signal the model to wrap up. The injection
still happens at exactly token N with zero warning. The model gets no time to
finish its current thought before the `</think>` boundary.

Graceful termination before the cutoff is expected to improve reasoning
performance. See Motivation and Possible Implementation for details.


### Motivation

Raw truncation of the thinking trace measurably reduces answer quality compared
to graceful termination. Muennighoff et al. (s1: Simple test-time scaling,
arXiv:2501.19393) showed that appending an end-of-thinking delimiter with
"Final Answer:" before the hard cut outperforms naïve truncation. This was
confirmed by follow-up work (arXiv:2505.05315), which states directly that
"the S1 approach performs better than directly truncating the full reasoning
trajectory, underscoring the importance of preserving the solution segment."

The current --reasoning-budget-message implementation injects a wrap-up message
at exactly token N, leaving the model zero tokens to actually act on it. This is
functionally equivalent to truncation with a cosmetic suffix — the model cannot
produce a meaningful conclusion within 0 remaining tokens.

### Possible Implementation

Three approaches in increasing complexity:

Option A — message offset
Inject the budget message at `budget - offset` instead of `budget`, giving the
model `offset` tokens to act on the wrap-up signal. The s1 paper
(https://arxiv.org/abs/2501.19393) shows this outperforms raw truncation.
Change in the COUNTING state of reasoning-budget.cpp:

    if (ctx->remaining <= ctx->warn_offset)  // was: <= 0

Files: reasoning-budget.cpp, reasoning-budget.h, common.h, arg.cpp,
sampling.cpp. Default 0 preserves current behavior.

Option B — separate budgeting
Split total budget into thinking (t) and conclusion (s) phases, t + s = budget.
Force `</think>` at token t, leave s tokens for a conclusion before the answer.
Follow-up work on s1 (https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.05315) shows this outperforms
the basic offset approach. Would add a second parameter, e.g.
--reasoning-budget-conclusion M.

Option C — logit biasing toward `</think>`
Ramp up the logit weight of `</think>` as the budget runs low, then force it at
the hard limit. No dependency on an injected phrase, model-agnostic. NVIDIA NIM
uses this approach with a 10% extension window for sentence completion. More
invasive (sampler changes) but cleanest long-term.

Options A and B build on the existing message injection architecture. Option C
is a parallel approach that could coexist with either.

Happy to test on ROCm/gfx1100 (Qwen3.5-27B) and contribute a draft of Option A
or B if there is interest.

Send the same deterministic long-prefix request three times. The following command uses

python3 - <<'PY'
import json

prompt = ("This is a deterministic long-context prefix for llama.cpp. " * 256).strip()

        "-H", "Content-Type: application/json",
        "-d", json.dumps(payload),
    ], text=True)
    print(f"response_{i+1}: {out}")
PY
```

repeated prefix. The server remained healthy and returned HTTP 200 for the requests, but the

response 2: "It seems like you're trying to test the limits of the AI's ability to"

items.title: [Bug]: [Store] BatchGet returns TRANSFER_FAIL at the 60 s wait while RDMA READs are still in flight; caller reuses the destination GPU buffers and gets corrupted KV
items.author: ThisFat
items.body_excerpt:
### Bug Report

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| Mooncake | `mooncake-transfer-engine` 0.3.13.post1 (PyPI wheel). Log line `transfer_task.cpp:891` matches tag `v0.3.13.post1` (commit `719735896c86`), i.e. the non-event-driven polling branch of `wait_for_completion()` |
| vLLM | 0.30.0, built-in `MooncakeStoreConnector`; `{"kv_connector":"MooncakeStoreConnector","kv_role":"kv_both","kv_load_failure_policy":"recompute","kv_connector_extra_config":{"lookup_async":true}}` |
| Model / serving | GLM-5.3-Flash (hybrid; `kv cache group sizes [640, 4, 640, 640, 640, 640]`), TP=8, `--max-model-len 262144`, `--enable-prefix-caching`, `--enable-chunked-prefill`, `--max-num-batched-tokens 8192`, `--prefix-match-unit 128` |
| Nodes | 3 nodes (A, B, C), each 8× NVIDIA H20-3e, 2× Xeon Platinum 8558P, 2 TiB RAM |
| OS / drivers | Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 5.15.0-187-generic, NVIDIA driver 610.43.02 with `nvidia_peermem` loaded, MLNX_OFED 24.10-5.1.6.1 |
| Python stack | Python 3.12.13, torch 2.13.0+cu130 |
| Network | RoCE v2, one ConnectX NIC per node for Mooncake (`mlx5_0`, 400 Gb/s NDR), netdev MTU 9000 / active MTU 4096, GID index 3 |
| Mooncake topology | `mooncake_master` on A: `--default_kv_lease_ttl=60s --eviction_high_watermark_ratio=0.85 --eviction_ratio=0.02`. One `mooncake_client` Store per node: `--protocol=rdma --device_names=mlx5_0 --global_segment_size=1099511627776 --local_buffer_size=8589934592 --metadata_server=P2PHANDSHAKE`. vLLM on each node uses the store as a client. Pool ~84% used, eviction continuously active |
| Env vars | No `MC_*` set (defaults: `MC_SLICE_TIMEOUT=-1`, `MC_RETRY_CNT=9`) |

### Description

`TransferEngineOperationState::wait_for_completion()` gives up after a hard-coded 60 s, sets `TRANSFER_FAIL` and returns, without cancelling or draining the batch. `Client::BatchGet` then returns to the caller. vLLM's `MooncakeStoreConnector` treats the failure as "these blocks are invalid": the scheduler reschedules the request and the GPU KV blocks are freed and reallocated (to other requests, or to the same request for recompute). The RDMA READs of the timed-out batch that are still queued or in flight keep the old local destination addresses. When they complete later, they write stale KV into GPU blocks that now hold other data.

This is the read-side counterpart of #4491 (timed-out put overwrites the next object).

**Expected:** after `BatchGet` returns an error for a key, Mooncake no longer writes into that key's destination buffer, or the API tells the caller the buffer is not yet safe to reuse.

**Actual:** `TRANSFER_FAIL` is returned while transfers targeting the buffer may still complete. The batch's `freeBatchID()` fails silently, and nothing in the logs shows that transfers were left behind.

### Observed behavior

1. After node C's Store joined the pool (2 → 3 TiB), all three vLLM processes started logging bursts of:

   ```
   E.... transfer_task.cpp:891] Failed to complete transfers after 60000 milliseconds for batch ...
   E.... client_service.cpp:...] Transfer failed for key: <key> with error: -800
   W.... client_service.cpp:...] lease_expired_before_data_transfer_completed key=<key>
   E.... real_client.cpp:...] BatchGet failed for key '<key>': LEASE_EXPIRED   (or TRANSFER_FAIL)
   WARNING [worker.py:1471] Failed to get N Mooncake keys from sub-batch (...)
   WARNING [scheduler.py:3240] Recovered from KV load failure: 1 request(s) rescheduled (N tokens affected).
   ```

   Over ~3.3 days: node A 8,825 timed-out batches, node B 5,849, node C 35,166. Nodes A and B had **zero** of these in the preceding 3 days with a 1- and then 2-Store pool (including ~18 h of A↔B cross-node reads). Load does not explain it: a day peaking at ~1.2 TB/h of `load_get` had none; a later day peaking at ~0.33 TB/h still had >1,000 timed-out batches per hour on node A.

2. No RDMA-level errors in the same logs: no `Process failed for slice`, no `Cannot redispatch slice`, no `BatchID cannot be freed`. `LEASE_EXPIRED` outnumbers `TRANSFER_FAIL` about 3:1, so many of these transfers did finish, just after 60 s.

3. Output corruption correlates with the timeouts. Over two days we matched every `Recovered from KV load failure` event (tokens > 0) to gateway requests on the same node (arrived before the event, first token after it, prompt ≥ affected tokens). An output counts as broken if it is garbled from the first token or runs away (hits `max_tokens` or ends in endless repetition):

   | Group (prompt ≥ 40k tokens) | Requests | Broken outputs |
   |---|---|---|
   | Rescheduled after a KV load failure | 169 | 6 (3.55%), garbled **from the first token** |
   | Same node, prefill overlapping the 60 s before a timeout, not rescheduled | 588 | 5 (0.85%), normal start, runaway later |
   | Same nodes, other times | 46,365 | 79 (0.17%) |
   | Nodes without Mooncake | 89,196 | 56 (0.06%) |

   The second row was never touched by the scheduler's recovery path, yet breaks ~5× more often than baseline. That points to memory being overwritten, not to a scheduling bug. Example: one request (49,713-token prompt, clean conversation history) waited 81.7 s for its first token. About 60 s after it arrived, the log on that node shows `Failed to get 65 Mooncake keys` → `rescheduled (49152 tokens affected)`, and the response was garbage from the first token.

4. Mitigation in progress: we stopped node C's Store (back to 2 Stores). The timeout and reschedule counters on A and B have not increased since.

### Steps to reproduce

**A. How it happened in production (reproduces for us, but not on demand)**

1. Start `mooncake_master` on node A with the flags above, and one `mooncake_client` Store (1 TiB, RDMA) on each of A, B, C.
2. Start vLLM 0.30.0 on each node with the `MooncakeStoreConnector` config above (`kv_load_failure_policy=recompute`, `lookup_async=true`).

items.title: [Roadmap] Further Ngram Speculative Decoding Support
items.author: kpham-sgl
items.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Ngram speculative decoding ([paper](https://arxiv.org/pdf/2312.12728)): during generation, previously decoded tokens are inserted into a trie. Before each forward pass, the trie is queried with the current suffix to produce a draft token tree, constructed via BFS (recency) or priority queue (frequency). The target model then verifies the entire tree in one pass. No draft model needed.

## Limitations

1. **No external corpus support.** The trie is only populated from the current decoding session's output tokens. Ngram speculative decoding works best with a large reference corpus, but there is currently no mechanism to load one.

2. **Insert path does not scale to long inputs.** It builds trie paths for almost every suffix, leading to near-O(n²) memory growth; when capacity is full, eviction can only remove leaf nodes and may fail.

## Goals

1. Support external corpus lookup
2. Scale to long input prefills

## Work Items

### Refactor

- [x] Split monolithic C++ ngram module into separate files — [PR #20393](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/20393) 
- [x] Rename `branch_length` to `max_trie_depth`- [PR #21181](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21181)
- [x] Remove `max_match_window_size` and `min_match_window_size` to match all suffixes in the trie - [PR #21225](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21225)
- [x] Maintain per-anchor matching state across decode steps — advance anchors on each new token instead of re-walking from trie root - [PR #21243](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21243)
- [x] Fix race condition in `TrieCache::insert()` when the worker thread's queue is empty - [PR #21186](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21186)
- [x] Replace busy-wait polling in `Ngram<Cache>::synchronize()` with a condition variable - [PR #21186](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21186)

### Adaptive Spec Dec
- [ ] https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/23629
### Spec V2
- [x] Ngram Spec V2 (require `top_k > 1` and optionally `page_size > 1` for Ngram) [PR #17260](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/17260)

### New Features

- [x] Load an external corpus (pre-specified format) via a server arg and build a [Suffix Automaton (SAM)](https://cp-algorithms.com/string/suffix-automaton.html) over it - [PR #21425](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/21425)
- [x] Support multiple SAMs with dynamic add/remove via HTTP API - [PR #22203](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22203)
- [x] Enhance support for mult-SAMs - [PR #22294](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22294) [PR #22471 ](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22471)
- [x] Accept length benchmark: output-as-corpus proves SAM ≥2x accept length boost - [PR #22199](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22199)
- [ ] Better solution for `combineResults`. Instead of relying on fixed `external_sam_budget`, use weighted dynamic allocation for Trie, SAM(s) match tokens based on longer matching / recency / frequency. - [PR #22538](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22538)
- [ ] Accept length benchmark: output-as-corpus and irrelevant corpora proves dynamic allocation work - [PR #22569](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22569)
- [ ] Per-request Trie [PR #22737](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/22737)
- [ ] Expand SAM match length (currently still cap by `max_trie_depth`)
- [ ] SAM for user request's input
- [ ] User request take in corpus_ids to match
- [ ] Transport SAM across scheduler in multi-scheduler system (disagg, DP, etc)
- [ ] Support DP Attention with Ngram [PR #28616](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/28616)
